nodes_add.name: Balak Singh of Hazro
nodes_add.note: Teacher at Hazro (Attock district, now Pakistan) who taught repetition of God's name above all ritual. Birth given as 1785 (Namdhari site, Dharam Singh), 1797 (Britannica) or 1799 (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism); died 1862. Namdharis count him as Guru after Gobind Singh.

nodes_add.name: Bhagat Jawahar Mal
nodes_add.note: Hazro devotee said by English Wikipedia to have greatly influenced Balak Singh. Dates unknown; single source.

nodes_add.name: Satguru Hari Singh
nodes_add.note: Born Budh Singh, Ram Singh's younger brother; named to lead by Ram Singh's written edict from Burma in 1875 (Namdhari account); led 1875-1906.

nodes_add.name: Satguru Partap Singh
nodes_add.note: Namdhari head 1906-1959 (Namdhari site: 53 years). Birth year not verified (site prints 1890, apparently in error).

nodes_add.name: Satguru Jagjit Singh
nodes_add.note: Elder son of Partap Singh; Namdhari head from 1959; 1920-2012, died 13 December 2012 (Namdhari site).

nodes_add.name: Satguru Uday Singh
nodes_add.note: Son of Bir Singh, nephew of Jagjit Singh; head at Sri Bhaini Sahib from 22 December 2012, appointed per The Tribune by Jagjit Singh's widow Chand Kaur. Born 1958 per Namdhari site.

nodes_add.name: Thakur Dalip Singh
nodes_add.note: Elder brother of Uday Singh; heads the Sirsa-based Namdhari faction that opposed Uday Singh's appointment in 2012 (The Tribune, 2016).

nodes_update.name: Satguru Ram Singh
nodes_update.note: b. 3 Feb 1816 Bhaini Araian, Ludhiana; met Balak Singh 1841; Namdhari code laid down Baisakhi 1857 (14 April per Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, 12 April per the Namdhari site and The Tribune); deported 18 Jan 1872 after the Malerkotla executions; d. 29 Nov 1885 Mergui per British records. Namdharis hold that he did not die.

edges_upsert.note: Sikh scripture, nam simran and Khalsa ideals; Namdharis also count him in a continuing line of living Gurus, which mainstream Sikhs reject.
Namdhari belief that Guru Gobind Singh lived in seclusion until 1812 and passed the guruship to Balak Singh. Rejected by mainstream Sikh bodies.
Met 1841 while Ram Singh served in Nau Nihal Singh's regiment (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism); Namdhari account says Balak Singh initiated him and passed the mantle.
Named by written edict from Burma (Namdhari site). Also his younger brother.
Nephew; appointed after Jagjit Singh's death per The Tribune (2016). Disputed by Thakur Dalip Singh's faction.
Rival Sirsa-based faction rejects Uday Singh's succession. The basis of its claim was not found in sources consulted.

English Wikipedia (Satguru Balak Singh), citing the Sikh Encyclopedia, Kirpal Singh's life of Jaimal Singh (2006) and RSSB's Heaven on Earth (1986): Jaimal Singh, later of Beas, visited Balak Singh in 1854 and asked about the Panch Shabad; Balak Singh is reported as saying they recite only the four-letter Naam. Not checked against the books.

places.name: Sri Bhaini Sahib
places.what: Birthplace (1816); code of conduct laid down at Baisakhi 1857; Namdhari headquarters

places.name: Hazro
places.what: Balak Singh's town, where Ram Singh met him (1841)

places.name: Malerkotla

glossary.def: Remembrance of the divine Name; in Sikh and Namdhari practice the steady, often silent repetition of a name of God such as Vaheguru.
The Guru's mantra. In Namdhari initiation the name Vaheguru, spoken into the initiate's ear.
Shouter; the popular and British name for the Namdharis, from the ecstatic cries (kuk) of their hymn singing.
Bearer of the Name; the Sikh movement led by Ram Singh from 1857, which holds that the line of living Gurus continues.
The Namdharis' name for their own initiated community.
True Guru. Namdharis use it as the title of each head of their line.
Province or governor; one of the district leaders Ram Singh appointed to organise his followers.
The book of the Tenth, writings attributed to Guru Gobind Singh. Namdharis honour it equally with the Guru Granth Sahib.
Sovereignty; a title used for the Sikh Gurus (First Patshahi, Tenth Patshahi). The Akal Takht reserved it for them in 2013.
The Sikh code of conduct issued by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, which defines a Sikh by belief in the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib.

issues: ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: number executed at Malerkotla differs: 49 on 17 Jan and 16 on 18 Jan (Daily Pioneer, Tribune), 66 commemorated by Namdharis (Tribune headline), about 65 (Britannica), 68 on 17 Jan (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism). All given in text. The brief's figure of 66 is the commemorative count.

ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: who ordered the 16 executions of 18 January (Cowan or Forsyth) not established from sources read; text says only that sixteen more died the next day and that both officers were removed.

ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: date of the move from Rangoon to Mergui not found. Encyclopaedia of Sikhism and an allaboutsikhs 'today in history' page place his confinement and death in Rangoon; Britannica and English Wikipedia give Mergui as the place of death. Text follows Mergui.
ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: founding date 14 April 1857 (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism) vs 12 April 1857 (The Tribune); both given.
ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: the brief mentions 'wedding reforms'. No verified cost figure (e.g. rupee amount) was found; the 1863 Khote start rests on English Wikipedia only.

ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: Namdhari self-description as Khalsa (Britannica, Namdhari site 'Sant Khalsa') conflicts with SikhiWiki (written from a critical standpoint), which says they consider themselves Sikhs but not Khalsa and reject khande di pahul. Text uses the movement's own term only.
ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: the statement that Namdhari sources describe no inner sound current or map of regions is an absence-of-evidence claim based on the sources consulted.
batch o27 places: Sri Bhaini Sahib coordinates are approximate and not verified (set verified: false).
Uday Singh's birth year 1958 rests on the Namdhari site only; Hari Singh's 1819 birth also from the Namdhari site.

sound-and-light.mdx: says Ram Singh began the movement 'a few years before Agra' (1857 vs 1861), consistent with shiv-dayal-singh.mdx. Ayya Vaikundar and Lalaji/Babuji fit the Word/Light question loosely; the intro describes them by what their pages say without forcing them into the theme.

ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: who ordered the 16 executions of 18 January is unresolved. History Today and Mathew Lyons name Cowan for the 49 of 17 January; English Wikipedia (Malerkotla) says Cowan and Forsyth ordered the executions; Wikipedia (Forsyth) says Forsyth supported Cowan's action. Text now says accounts differ. A scholarly source (Bajwa 1965) should settle it.
ram-singh-namdhari.mdx: Mergui transfer date still not found; EoS mentions only Rangoon and gives no place of death. Text keeps Mergui as the British record and notes Rangoon-only accounts.

thakur-dalip-singh node: CBI case removed under living-person caution. Facts on record: The Tribune (26 June 2021) reports he was named an accused by the CBI in an alleged Nov-Dec 2015 conspiracy to kill Uday Singh with a blast at a Jalandhar music festival (IPC 120B, 304, Explosive Substances Act, Arms Act, UAPA); Mohali CBI court issued a non-bailable warrant in June 2021. Single report; no response from him found; later status unknown. Author to decide if a later, multi-sourced account justifies including it.
thakur-dalip-singh: basis of his faction's claim to succession not found in sources consulted.

Chand Kaur murder: 2019 HT headline reports a first CBI arrest; a 2023 Tribune report quotes a justice society saying no arrest had been made. Text says only that no one had been convicted as of 2023.

ram-singh-namdhari: Born 3 Feb 1816, Bhaini Araian, eldest of four children of Jassa Singh and Sada Kaur; joined Ranjit Singh's army at 20 in Nau Nihal Singh's regiment; met Balak Singh 1841 -> https://eos.learnpunjabi.org/RAM%20SINGH%20BABA%20(1816-1885).html
Quote 'On Baisakhi day, 14 April 1857, he laid down the code of conduct for his followers.'; code forbade meat, drink, tomb worship; 22 subas -> https://www.allaboutsikhs.com/ram-singh-baba/

Founding 12 April 1857 at Bhaini Sahib; 49 executed first day, 16 next day; 66 in headline; Cowan; boycotts of services, goods, schools, courts -> https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/anniversary/namdhari-shaheedi-diwas-66-kukas-executed-by-cannon/amp
16 more blown from cannon on 18 January 1872 -> https://www.dailypioneer.com/2015/state-editions/heroic-sacrifice-of-namdharis-blown-up-by-cannons.html

Malodh raid 14 Jan, Malerkotla 15 Jan; 49 executed 17 Jan; Cowan dismissed; Ram Singh had warned authorities; deported to Rangoon -> https://mathewlyons.co.uk/2024/04/09/a-sikh-uprising-against-the-british-empire-the-kuka-revolt-of-1872/
49 executed by cannon 17 January 1872; about 200 Namdhari -> https://www.historytoday.com/archive/months-past/indias-kuka-revolt-ends-death
Inquiry removed both Forsyth and Cowan -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Douglas_Forsyth

1871 Amritsar (4 killed, 14 June) and Raikot (3 killed); 8 policemen killed at Malerkotla; 68 blown from guns; Allahabad then Rangoon under Bengal Act of 1818; died 29 Nov 1885 -> https://eos.learnpunjabi.org/RAM%20SINGH%20BABA%20(1816-1885).html

Exiled 18 Jan 1872; British death record 29 Nov 1885 Mergui; Rangoon telegram 8 Dec 1885; Jaswinder Singh and Charles Bernard letter 23 Aug 1886; Namdharis believe he is alive and will return; white robes, wool rosaries; anand karaj from Khote 1863; amrit to women; opposed infanticide, child marriage, sale of girls; kuk -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satguru_Ram_Singh
Born 1816 Bhaini, died 1885 Mergui; 'first Indian to use noncooperation and boycott' -> https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ram-Singh

Balak Singh quote 'did not believe in any religious ritual other than the repetition of God's name'; white handwoven cloth; straight turban; Dasam Granth equal; living Guru lineage; about 65 executed -> https://www.britannica.com/topic/Namdhari
Balak Singh dates 1785/1797/1799 variants, d. 1862; Jawahar Mal; patasha, coconut, five paise, five circumambulations -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satguru_Balak_Singh
